are allergic to amphetamine products or any of the ingredients in Adderall (see ingredients below)

heart problems, heart disease, heart defects, or high blood pressure, or a family history of sudden death or heart problems

kidney or liver problems
seizures or an abnormal brain wave test (EEG)
circulation problems in the fingers or toes

subject: Amlodipine besylate
relation_definition: The subject drug leads to or results in the effect or condition specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Amlodipine besylate is a prescription medicine.
It is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension).
It is used to prevent certain types of angina (chest pain).
It belongs to a class of medications called calcium channel blockers.
Amlodipine besylate works by relaxing and widening the blood vessels.
This causes blood to flow more easily.
This improves blood pressure.
Amlodipine besylate controls angina chest pain by increasing the supply of blood to the heart.
If taken regularly, this medicine controls chest pain.
It does not stop chest pain once it starts.
Your doctor may prescribe a different medication to take when you have chest pain.
Amlodipine is also used alone or in combination with other medicines to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) in adults and children at least 6 years old.
Lowering blood pressure may lower your risk of a stroke or heart attack.
Amlodipine besylate is available as:
Amlodipine 5 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 10 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 2.5 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 1 mg/mL solution (Norliqva)

It is used to prevent certain types of angina (chest pain).
It belongs to a class of medications called calcium channel blockers.
Amlodipine besylate works by relaxing and widening the blood vessels.
This causes blood to flow more easily.
This improves blood pressure.
Amlodipine besylate controls angina chest pain by increasing the supply of blood to the heart.
If taken regularly, this medicine controls chest pain.
It does not stop chest pain once it starts.
Your doctor may prescribe a different medication to take when you have chest pain.
Amlodipine is also used alone or in combination with other medicines to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) in adults and children at least 6 years old.
Lowering blood pressure may lower your risk of a stroke or heart attack.
Amlodipine besylate is available as:
Amlodipine 5 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 10 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 2.5 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 1 mg/mL solution (Norliqva)

Common amoxicillin side effects:
Common amoxicillin side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or rash.
These side effects affected more than 1% of patients in clinical trials.
Serious amoxicillin side effects:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin.
Signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
severe stomach pain or vomiting (which may be signs of a serious intestinal condition); or
diarrhea that is watery or bloody (even if it occurs months after your last dose).
This is not a complete list of side effects.
Others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may also report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

subject: amoxicillin
relation_definition: The subject drug has a specific effect or behavior in the group of individuals specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Amoxicillin is a penicillin antibiotic.
Amoxicillin is used to treat bacterial infections.
The infections include tonsillitis, bronchitis, sinusitis, pneumonia, and infections of the ear, nose, throat, skin, or urinary tract.
Amoxicillin clavulanate is a combination of amoxicillin and clavulanate potassium.
The amoxicillin fights bacteria.
The clavulanate potassium helps prevent certain bacteria from becoming resistant to amoxicillin.
Amoxicillin is sometimes used together with another antibiotic called clarithromycin (Biaxin).
This combination is used to treat stomach ulcers.
The ulcers are caused by Helicobacter pylori infection.
This combination is sometimes used with a stomach acid reducer called lansoprazole (Prevacid).
Amoxicillin 500mg and 250mg are available as tablets or capsules and as an oral suspension.
Many brands and forms of amoxicillin are available.
Not all brands are listed on this leaflet.

Common amoxicillin side effects:
Common amoxicillin side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or rash.
These side effects affected more than 1% of patients in clinical trials.
Serious amoxicillin side effects:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin.
Signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
severe stomach pain or vomiting (which may be signs of a serious intestinal condition); or
diarrhea that is watery or bloody (even if it occurs months after your last dose).
This is not a complete list of side effects.
Others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may also report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

evidence_text:
Amoxicillin is a penicillin antibiotic.
Amoxicillin is used to treat bacterial infections.
The infections include tonsillitis, bronchitis, sinusitis, pneumonia, and infections of the ear, nose, throat, skin, or urinary tract.
Amoxicillin clavulanate is a combination of amoxicillin and clavulanate potassium.
The amoxicillin fights bacteria.
The clavulanate potassium helps prevent certain bacteria from becoming resistant to amoxicillin.
Amoxicillin is sometimes used together with another antibiotic called clarithromycin (Biaxin).
This combination is used to treat stomach ulcers.
The ulcers are caused by Helicobacter pylori infection.
This combination is sometimes used with a stomach acid reducer called lansoprazole (Prevacid).
Amoxicillin 500mg and 250mg are available as tablets or capsules and as an oral suspension.
Many brands and forms of amoxicillin are available.
Not all brands are listed on this leaflet.

evidence_text:
Do not use this medication if you are allergic to amoxicillin.
Do not use this medication if you are allergic to any other penicillin antibiotic.
Examples of other penicillin antibiotics include ampicillin, dicloxacillin, oxacillin, and penicillin.
Other penicillin antibiotics include ampicillin (Omnipen, Principen), dicloxacillin (Dycill, Dynapen), oxacillin (Bactocill), and penicillin (Beepen-VK, Ledercillin VK, Pen-V, Pen-Vee K, Pfizerpen, V-Cillin K, Veetids).
Before using amoxicillin, tell your doctor if you are allergic to cephalosporins.
Examples of cephalosporins include Omnicef, Cefzil, Ceftin, and Keflex.
There are other cephalosporins as well.
Also, tell your doctor if you have asthma.
Tell your doctor if you have liver disease.
Tell your doctor if you have kidney disease.
Tell your doctor if you have a bleeding or blood-clotting disorder.
Tell your doctor if you have mononucleosis (also called "mono").
Tell your doctor if you have any type of allergy.
Amoxicillin can make birth control pills less effective.

Atorvastatin works by selectively blocking HMG-CoA reductase.
HMG-CoA reductase is the key enzyme the liver uses to produce cholesterol.
By slowing this process, it reduces cholesterol production in the liver.
It increases the number of LDL receptors on liver cells.
This helps remove more LDL ("bad") cholesterol from the bloodstream.
As a result, it lowers overall LDL levels.
It decreases the number of LDL particles.
It improves the body's ability to clear cholesterol.

For adults and pediatric patients (10 years and older) with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia.

evidence_text:
Bupropion is an antidepressant medication used to treat depression and seasonal affective disorder.
It also supports smoking cessation and weight management.
Bupropion is the active ingredient in Wellbutrin and Zyban.
Auvelity contains bupropion and dextromethorphan.
Contrave contains bupropion and naltrexone.
Bupropion improves mood regulation.
Bupropion improves nicotine cravings.
When combined with naltrexone, bupropion helps reduce food intake.
Bupropion is thought to work by changing levels of certain chemicals in the brain.
These chemicals include noradrenaline and dopamine.
Bupropion first became an FDA-approved medicine on 30 December 1985.

subject: CYP2B6 inducers
relation_definition: The subject drug should be taken or used in the manner specified by the object entity (for example with food or at a fixed time).
evidence_text:
You may have a higher risk of seizures if you use certain other medicines while taking bupropion.
Many drugs can interact with bupropion.
Tell your doctor about all medicines you use, and those you start or stop using during your treatment.
This includes prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Some examples of drugs that interact with bupropion are:
Digoxin: May decrease plasma digoxin levels.
Monitor digoxin levels
MAOIs: Increased risk of hypertensive reactions can occur when used concomitantly with this medication.
Drugs that lower seizure threshold: Dose bupropion with caution.
Medicines that are CYP2B6 inducers may require a dose increase if coadministered with other CYP2B6 inducers.
Examples of CYP2B6 inducers include ritonavir, lopinavir, efavirenz, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, and phenytoin.
Dose increases should be based on clinical response.
Dose increases should not exceed the maximum recommended dose.
Medicines that are CYP2B6 inhibitors may require dose adjustment if coadministered with CYP2B6 inhibitors.

subject: Flonase Nasal Spray
relation_definition: The subject drug is obtainable through the method or authority specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Flonase is a nasal spray containing fluticasone propionate.
Fluticasone propionate is a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation in the lining of the nose.
Flonase Nasal Spray is used to treat nasal congestion, sneezing, runny nose, and itchy or watery eyes.
These symptoms are caused by seasonal or year-round allergies.
Flonase Allergy Relief is for use in adults and children who are at least 4 years old.
It is available without a prescription.
Children's Flonase Allergy Relief contains the same medicine.
It is also for ages 4 and older.
Flonase Sensimist contains fluticasone furoate rather than fluticasone propionate.
It is approved for use in adults and children 2 years of age and older.
Children's Flonase Sensimist is also for ages 2 and older.
In Flonase Sensimist labeling, relief of itchy, watery eyes applies to ages 12 and older.
The brand-name prescription version of Flonase nasal spray has been discontinued in the United States.
Generic fluticasone propionate nasal spray is still available by prescription.

How long does fluoxetine take to work?
:
Most people need to take fluoxetine for 4 to 6 weeks before feeling the full effects.
Some improvement in sleep, appetite, or energy levels may be noticeable within the first 1 to 2 weeks.
Mood and motivation typically take longer to improve.
For obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), it may take 5 weeks or longer to see the full benefit.
It is important to keep taking this medicine as prescribed.
You should continue even if you do not feel immediate improvement.
Do not stop without speaking to your doctor first.
Is fluoxetine a controlled substance?
:
No, fluoxetine is not a controlled substance.
It is not classified under the DEA Controlled Substances Act.
This means it does not have recognized potential for dependence or abuse.
Drugs like opioids or benzodiazepines have this potential.
It is, however, a prescription-only medicine.
It still requires a valid prescription from a licensed healthcare provider.
Is fluoxetine an SSRI?
:
Yes, fluoxetine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI).

evidence_text:
Is 40mg of fluoxetine a high dose?
40mg of fluoxetine is considered a moderate maintenance dose in adults for major depressive disorder (MDD) and OCD.
The standard starting dose for most conditions is 20mg per day.
The starting dose for panic disorder is 10mg.
If symptoms have not improved after several weeks, the dose may be increased.
The dose may be increased up to 40mg for MDD and OCD.
The dose may be increased up to 20mg for panic disorder.
The recommended dose for bulimia is 60mg per day.
Your doctor will determine the right dose for you based on your condition and response to treatment.
Does fluoxetine cause weight gain?
:
Fluoxetine is less likely to cause weight gain than many other antidepressants.
In the short term, it can actually cause mild weight loss.
This is due to reduced appetite.
Reduced appetite is one of its common side effects.
However, some people do experience weight changes over longer-term use.
If you notice significant weight changes while taking this medicine, speak to your doctor.
Dose adjustments or alternative treatments may be available.

How long does fluoxetine stay in your system?
:
Fluoxetine stays in your system longer than most other antidepressants.
After stopping this medicine, it takes approximately 1 to 4 days for the drug itself to be reduced by half.
Fluoxetine converts in the body to an active metabolite called norfluoxetine.
Norfluoxetine has a much longer half-life of 4 to 16 days.
This means this medicine and its active metabolite can remain detectable in your system.
They can remain detectable for up to 5 weeks.
This duration is after your last dose.
This is clinically important for two reasons:
Switching medications requires a washout period.
This applies if you are switching from fluoxetine to certain other antidepressants.
These other antidepressants include MAOIs.
Your doctor will require a washout period of at least 5 weeks.
This period allows fluoxetine to fully clear your system.
This avoids dangerous drug interactions.
Stopping fluoxetine.

How long does fluoxetine take to work?
:
Most people need to take fluoxetine for 4 to 6 weeks before feeling the full effects.
Some improvement in sleep, appetite, or energy levels may be noticeable within the first 1 to 2 weeks.
Mood and motivation typically take longer to improve.
For obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), it may take 5 weeks or longer to see the full benefit.
It is important to keep taking this medicine as prescribed.
You should continue even if you do not feel immediate improvement.
Do not stop without speaking to your doctor first.
Is fluoxetine a controlled substance?
:
No, fluoxetine is not a controlled substance.
It is not classified under the DEA Controlled Substances Act.
This means it does not have recognized potential for dependence or abuse.
Drugs like opioids or benzodiazepines have this potential.
It is, however, a prescription-only medicine.
It still requires a valid prescription from a licensed healthcare provider.
Is fluoxetine an SSRI?
:
Yes, fluoxetine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI).

Tell your healthcare provider if you are pregnant, become pregnant, or plan to become pregnant while taking fluoxetine tablets.
Using fluoxetine later in pregnancy may increase the risk of complications in the newborn.
Some complications require a longer hospital stay.
Some complications require breathing support.
Some complications require tube feeding.
A serious complication is a lung condition called persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN).
Untreated depression carries risks in pregnancy.
Discuss the benefits and risks of treatment with your healthcare provider.
Do not stop treatment on your own.
If you become pregnant while taking fluoxetine tablets, ask your healthcare provider about joining the National Pregnancy Registry for Antidepressants.
The registry tracks pregnancy outcomes in women who take these medicines.
You can enroll by calling 1-866-961-2388 or visiting womensmentalhealth.org.
Breastfeeding:
Fluoxetine passes into breast milk.
Tell your healthcare provider if you are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed.

evidence_text:
How long does fluoxetine take to work?
:
Most people need to take fluoxetine for 4 to 6 weeks before feeling the full effects.
Some improvement in sleep, appetite, or energy levels may be noticeable within the first 1 to 2 weeks.
Mood and motivation typically take longer to improve.
For obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), it may take 5 weeks or longer to see the full benefit.
It is important to keep taking this medicine as prescribed.
You should continue even if you do not feel immediate improvement.
Do not stop without speaking to your doctor first.
Is fluoxetine a controlled substance?
:
No, fluoxetine is not a controlled substance.
It is not classified under the DEA Controlled Substances Act.
This means it does not have recognized potential for dependence or abuse.
Drugs like opioids or benzodiazepines have this potential.
It is, however, a prescription-only medicine.
It still requires a valid prescription from a licensed healthcare provider.
Is fluoxetine an SSRI?
:
Yes, fluoxetine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI).

How long does fluoxetine take to work?
:
Most people need to take fluoxetine for 4 to 6 weeks before feeling the full effects.
Some improvement in sleep, appetite, or energy levels may be noticeable within the first 1 to 2 weeks.
Mood and motivation typically take longer to improve.
For obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), it may take 5 weeks or longer to see the full benefit.
It is important to keep taking this medicine as prescribed.
You should continue even if you do not feel immediate improvement.
Do not stop without speaking to your doctor first.
Is fluoxetine a controlled substance?
:
No, fluoxetine is not a controlled substance.
It is not classified under the DEA Controlled Substances Act.
This means it does not have recognized potential for dependence or abuse.
Drugs like opioids or benzodiazepines have this potential.
It is, however, a prescription-only medicine.
It still requires a valid prescription from a licensed healthcare provider.
Is fluoxetine an SSRI?
:
Yes, fluoxetine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI).

Fluoxetine is FDA-approved to treat the following conditions:
Major depressive disorder (MDD) for acute and maintenance treatment in adults and children aged 8 years and older
Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) for acute and maintenance treatment in adults and children aged 7 years and older
Bulimia nervosa for acute and maintenance treatment of binge-eating and purging in adults with moderate to severe bulimia
Panic disorder for the treatment of panic attacks in adults
When used in combination with olanzapine, fluoxetine is also FDA-approved for:
Acute treatment of depressive episodes associated with Bipolar I disorder (depressive episodes) in adults and children aged 10 years and older
Treatment-resistant depression for adults who have not responded to at least two adequate antidepressant trials
Fluoxetine alone is not approved for bipolar I depressive episodes or treatment-resistant depression.
Olanzapine must be used in combination for these indications.

How long does fluoxetine take to work?
:
Most people need to take fluoxetine for 4 to 6 weeks before feeling the full effects.
Some improvement in sleep, appetite, or energy levels may be noticeable within the first 1 to 2 weeks.
Mood and motivation typically take longer to improve.
For obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), it may take 5 weeks or longer to see the full benefit.
It is important to keep taking this medicine as prescribed.
You should continue even if you do not feel immediate improvement.
Do not stop without speaking to your doctor first.
Is fluoxetine a controlled substance?
:
No, fluoxetine is not a controlled substance.
It is not classified under the DEA Controlled Substances Act.
This means it does not have recognized potential for dependence or abuse.
Drugs like opioids or benzodiazepines have this potential.
It is, however, a prescription-only medicine.
It still requires a valid prescription from a licensed healthcare provider.
Is fluoxetine an SSRI?
:
Yes, fluoxetine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI).

How long does fluoxetine stay in your system?

Fluoxetine stays in your system longer than most other antidepressants.
After stopping this medicine, it takes approximately 1 to 4 days for the drug itself to be reduced by half.
Fluoxetine converts in the body to an active metabolite called norfluoxetine.

Switching medications requires a washout period.

subject: reabsorption of serotonin
relation_definition: The subject condition or entity is defined by the description specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Fluoxetine works by blocking the reabsorption of serotonin in the brain.
This process leaves more serotonin active between nerve cells.

How long does fluoxetine stay in your system?
:
Fluoxetine stays in your system longer than most other antidepressants.
After stopping this medicine, it takes approximately 1 to 4 days for the drug itself to be reduced by half.
Fluoxetine converts in the body to an active metabolite called norfluoxetine.
Norfluoxetine has a much longer half-life of 4 to 16 days.
This means this medicine and its active metabolite can remain detectable in your system.
They can remain detectable for up to 5 weeks.
This duration is after your last dose.
This is clinically important for two reasons:
Switching medications requires a washout period.
This applies if you are switching from fluoxetine to certain other antidepressants.
These other antidepressants include MAOIs.
Your doctor will require a washout period of at least 5 weeks.
This period allows fluoxetine to fully clear your system.
This avoids dangerous drug interactions.
Stopping fluoxetine.

evidence_text:
Fluoxetine is FDA-approved to treat the following conditions:
Major depressive disorder (MDD) for acute and maintenance treatment in adults and children aged 8 years and older
Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) for acute and maintenance treatment in adults and children aged 7 years and older
Bulimia nervosa for acute and maintenance treatment of binge-eating and purging in adults with moderate to severe bulimia
Panic disorder for the treatment of panic attacks in adults
When used in combination with olanzapine, fluoxetine is also FDA-approved for:
Acute treatment of depressive episodes associated with Bipolar I disorder (depressive episodes) in adults and children aged 10 years and older
Treatment-resistant depression for adults who have not responded to at least two adequate antidepressant trials
Fluoxetine alone is not approved for bipolar I depressive episodes or treatment-resistant depression.
Olanzapine must be used in combination for these indications.

subject: Gabapentin
object: resulting in a calmer, less excitable nerve circuit
relation_definition: The subject drug leads to or results in the effect or condition specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Gabapentin works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain and nervous system.
It does this by binding to the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels in nerve cells.
The alpha-2-delta subunit is thought to normalize chemical signals nerves send to each other.
This results in a calmer, less excitable nerve circuit.
That same effect helps in different ways depending on what gabapentin is treating:
Epilepsy - dampens the runaway electrical firing that causes seizures.
Postherpetic neuralgia (shingles nerve pain) - reduces the abnormal pain signals from nerves damaged by shingles.
Restless legs syndrome (gabapentin enacarbil / Horizant) has an exact mechanism that is less clear.
The same calming effect on overactive nerves is thought to ease the urge-to-move sensation.
Gabapentin is not an opioid, sedative, or anti-inflammatory painkiller.
It works directly on the nerves.
It helps nerve-related pain.
It isn't useful for everyday pain.
Everyday pain includes headaches.
Everyday pain includes sprains.

subject: Gabapentin
object: binding to the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels in nerve cells
relation_definition: The subject drug has a specific effect or behavior in the group of individuals specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Gabapentin works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain and nervous system.
It does this by binding to the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels in nerve cells.
The alpha-2-delta subunit is thought to normalize chemical signals nerves send to each other.
This results in a calmer, less excitable nerve circuit.
That same effect helps in different ways depending on what gabapentin is treating:
Epilepsy - dampens the runaway electrical firing that causes seizures.
Postherpetic neuralgia (shingles nerve pain) - reduces the abnormal pain signals from nerves damaged by shingles.
Restless legs syndrome (gabapentin enacarbil / Horizant) has an exact mechanism that is less clear.
The same calming effect on overactive nerves is thought to ease the urge-to-move sensation.
Gabapentin is not an opioid, sedative, or anti-inflammatory painkiller.
It works directly on the nerves.
It helps nerve-related pain.
It isn't useful for everyday pain.
Everyday pain includes headaches.
Everyday pain includes sprains.

anxiety medicines such as lorazepam and other benzodiazepines
muscle relaxers, sedatives, or other seizure medicines that cause drowsiness

evidence_text:
Gabapentin works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain and nervous system.
It does this by binding to the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels in nerve cells.
The alpha-2-delta subunit is thought to normalize chemical signals nerves send to each other.
This results in a calmer, less excitable nerve circuit.
That same effect helps in different ways depending on what gabapentin is treating:
Epilepsy - dampens the runaway electrical firing that causes seizures.
Postherpetic neuralgia (shingles nerve pain) - reduces the abnormal pain signals from nerves damaged by shingles.
Restless legs syndrome (gabapentin enacarbil / Horizant) has an exact mechanism that is less clear.
The same calming effect on overactive nerves is thought to ease the urge-to-move sensation.
Gabapentin is not an opioid, sedative, or anti-inflammatory painkiller.
It works directly on the nerves.
It helps nerve-related pain.
It isn't useful for everyday pain.
Everyday pain includes headaches.
Everyday pain includes sprains.

Taking gabapentin with other medicines can cause dangerous side effects.

The side effects include life-threatening breathing problems.
Ask your doctor before using gabapentin with:
opioid pain medicines such as hydrocodone, oxycodone, morphine, or buprenorphine
sleeping pills such as zolpidem
anxiety medicines such as lorazepam and other benzodiazepines
muscle relaxers, sedatives, or other seizure medicines that cause drowsiness
Avoid drinking alcohol while taking gabapentin, because it can add to these effects.

Take gabapentin at least 2 hours after an antacid.

This may increase drowsiness.
This may also increase the risk of breathing problems.
Your doctor may adjust your dose.
Gabapentin does not usually interact with other seizure medicines.

It is often called a water pill.
It is used to treat high blood pressure.

It works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body.
You urinate more.

It is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth.
It is usually taken once or twice a day.

oral tablet (12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg)
oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)

Esidrix (discontinued) was a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Microzide capsules (discontinued) were a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Now generic tablets and capsules are available.
The brand name of hydrochlorothiazide oral suspension is Inzirqo.
Hydrochlorothiazide is also an ingredient in many combination blood pressure medicines.

Hydrochlorothiazide is approved to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and fluid retention (edema) in certain patients.
High blood pressure:
HCTZ is used to manage high blood pressure (hypertension), either on its own or alongside other blood pressure medicines.
Lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of fatal and non-fatal cardiovascular events, mainly strokes and heart attacks.
All three forms of hydrochlorothiazide, tablets, capsules and the oral suspension, are approved for high blood pressure in adults.
The oral suspension is also approved for children.
Fluid retention:
Hydrochlorothiazide tablets are used to treat a build-up of fluid (edema) associated with:
congestive heart failure
cirrhosis of the liver
kidney conditions, including nephrotic syndrome, acute glomerulonephritis and chronic kidney failure
treatment with corticosteroid or estrogen medicines
The HCTZ oral suspension is approved for fluid retention.
The fluid retention is associated with congestive heart failure, cirrhosis of the liver, and kidney disease.
Kidney disease includes nephrotic syndrome.

With longer-term use, blood volume returns towards normal.
The blood vessels themselves offer less resistance to blood flow.
Hydrochlorothiazide does not usually change blood pressure that is already normal.

:

evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is approved to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and fluid retention (edema) in certain patients.
High blood pressure:
HCTZ is used to manage high blood pressure (hypertension), either on its own or alongside other blood pressure medicines.
Lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of fatal and non-fatal cardiovascular events, mainly strokes and heart attacks.
All three forms of hydrochlorothiazide, tablets, capsules and the oral suspension, are approved for high blood pressure in adults.
The oral suspension is also approved for children.
Fluid retention:
Hydrochlorothiazide tablets are used to treat a build-up of fluid (edema) associated with:
congestive heart failure
cirrhosis of the liver
kidney conditions, including nephrotic syndrome, acute glomerulonephritis and chronic kidney failure
treatment with corticosteroid or estrogen medicines
The HCTZ oral suspension is approved for fluid retention.
The fluid retention is associated with congestive heart failure, cirrhosis of the liver, and kidney disease.
Kidney disease includes nephrotic syndrome.

evidence_text:
Tell your doctor and pharmacist about all the medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Medicines that need particular care:
Lithium.
Lithium and diuretics generally should not be taken together.
Hydrochlorothiazide reduces how quickly the kidneys clear lithium.
This reduction carries a high risk of lithium toxicity.
Cholestyramine and colestipol.
These cholesterol-lowering resins bind hydrochlorothiazide in the gut.
They can reduce how much you absorb by up to 85 percent for cholestyramine and 43 percent for colestipol.
The doses need to be separated.
The label advises taking hydrochlorothiazide for the oral suspension.
The label advises taking hydrochlorothiazide at least 4 hours before the resin.
The label advises taking hydrochlorothiazide 4 to 6 hours after the resin.
NSAIDs such as ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), diclofenac, meloxicam, indomethacin, celecoxib and aspirin.
These can reduce the fluid-clearing and blood-pressure-lowering effects of hydrochlorothiazide.

evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is approved to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and fluid retention (edema) in certain patients.
High blood pressure:
HCTZ is used to manage high blood pressure (hypertension), either on its own or alongside other blood pressure medicines.
Lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of fatal and non-fatal cardiovascular events, mainly strokes and heart attacks.
All three forms of hydrochlorothiazide, tablets, capsules and the oral suspension, are approved for high blood pressure in adults.
The oral suspension is also approved for children.
Fluid retention:
Hydrochlorothiazide tablets are used to treat a build-up of fluid (edema) associated with:
congestive heart failure
cirrhosis of the liver
kidney conditions, including nephrotic syndrome, acute glomerulonephritis and chronic kidney failure
treatment with corticosteroid or estrogen medicines
The HCTZ oral suspension is approved for fluid retention.
The fluid retention is associated with congestive heart failure, cirrhosis of the liver, and kidney disease.
Kidney disease includes nephrotic syndrome.

Hydrochlorothiazide can lower the levels of potassium, sodium, magnesium and chloride in your blood.
Low potassium (hypokalemia) is the most common of these.
It is more likely at higher doses.
It is more likely during rapid fluid loss.
It is more likely if you have severe cirrhosis.
It is more likely after long-term use.
Your doctor will check your blood before you start and at intervals during treatment.
Contact your doctor if you have any of the following, which can be signs of a fluid or salt imbalance:
dry mouth, thirst, or unusual weakness or tiredness
drowsiness, restlessness or confusion
muscle pain, cramps or muscle fatigue
fast heartbeat
passing much less urine than usual
nausea or vomiting
seizures
Kidney and liver problems:
HCTZ reduces the fluid volume in your body.
This reduction can lead to sudden kidney injury.
The risk is higher if you have chronic kidney disease.
The risk is higher if you have heart failure.
The risk is higher if you are already low on fluid.

Hydrochlorothiazide works by inhibiting the kidneys from reabsorbing sodium and chloride.
More salt and water leave the body in the urine.
This helps reduce excess fluid buildup (edema).
Exactly how thiazides lower blood pressure is not fully understood.
The early effect is thought to come from a drop in blood volume.
With longer-term use, blood volume returns towards normal.
The blood vessels themselves offer less resistance to blood flow.
Hydrochlorothiazide does not usually change blood pressure that is already normal.
Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic.

Does hydrochlorothiazide cause weight loss?
:
Hydrochlorothiazide is not a weight loss medicine.
Some people see the number on the scales drop in the first days or weeks of treatment.
This is extra fluid leaving the body.
This is not any loss of body fat.
The weight loss levels off.
Do not take hydrochlorothiazide to lose weight.
Can you drink alcohol while taking hydrochlorothiazide?
:
Alcohol can make the drop in blood pressure that happens when you stand up worse.
This drop in blood pressure may leave you feeling dizzy or faint.
The same applies to barbiturates and opioid pain medicines.
Tell your doctor how much you drink so they can advise you.
Does hydrochlorothiazide lower your potassium?
:
Yes.
Hydrochlorothiazide can lower blood potassium.
This condition is known as hypokalemia.
This effect is more likely at higher doses.
This effect is more likely when fluid is lost quickly.
This effect is more likely if you have severe cirrhosis.
This effect is more likely after taking the medicine for a long time.
Your doctor will check your potassium with blood tests.

subject: Hydrochlorothiazide
relation_definition: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the disease or medical condition specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic.
It is often called a water pill.
It is used to treat high blood pressure.
It is used to reduce a build-up of fluid in the body.
This build-up of fluid is called edema.
It works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body.
You urinate more.
Hydrochlorothiazide is often shortened to HCTZ on prescriptions and medical records.
It is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth.
It is usually taken once or twice a day.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as:
oral tablet (12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg)
oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)
Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) brand names included HydroDIURIL tablets (discontinued).
Esidrix (discontinued) was a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Microzide capsules (discontinued) were a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Now generic tablets and capsules are available.
The brand name of hydrochlorothiazide oral suspension is Inzirqo.
Hydrochlorothiazide is also an ingredient in many combination blood pressure medicines.

Do not take hydrochlorothiazide if you are unable to pass urine (anuria).
Do not take hydrochlorothiazide if you are allergic to hydrochlorothiazide or to other sulfonamide-derived medicines (sometimes called sulfa drugs).
Before you start HCTZ, tell your doctor if you have or have ever had:
kidney disease or reduced kidney function
liver disease, including cirrhosis
diabetes
gout or high uric acid levels
high cholesterol or high triglycerides
high calcium levels or a parathyroid gland disorder
low potassium or low sodium levels
lupus (systemic lupus erythematosus)
glaucoma
an allergy to sulfa medicines or to penicillin
Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
Hydrochlorothiazide may cause jaundice or bleeding problems in a newborn.
The medicine can pass into breast milk.
The medicine may cause serious side effects in a nursing baby.
You and your doctor should decide whether you will take this medicine.
You and your doctor should decide whether you will breastfeed.

Your doctor will choose the smallest dose that controls your condition.
Your doctor may adjust the dose over time.
Follow your prescription label and do not change your dose yourself.
HCTZ dose for high blood pressure (adults):
Tablets: The starting dose is hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg once a day.
The dose may be increased to 50 mg a day.
The dose is taken as a single dose or split into two doses.
Doses above 50 mg a day are often associated with a marked drop in blood potassium.
Most people do not need more than 50 mg a day when hydrochlorothiazide is taken alongside other blood pressure medicines
The starting dose is a hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg capsule once a day.
It can be taken on its own or with other blood pressure medicines.
Total daily doses above 50 mg are not recommended.
Capsules are approved for high blood pressure only, not for fluid retention.
HCTZ dose for fluid retention (adults):
Tablets: The usual dose is hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg to 100 mg a day, taken as a single dose or split into two doses.
Many people with fluid retention respond to intermittent treatment.

Your doctor will use blood tests to check that your dose is right.
This is usually done 6 to 8 weeks after any dose change.

Children are tested more often.

They are also tested 2 weeks after any dose change.

This could lead to the wrong dose change.
Stop biotin and any biotin-containing supplements at least 2 days before a thyroid blood test.

lower the level of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) in the blood in people being treated for a certain type of thyroid cancer, alongside surgery and radioactive iodine therapy.

Levothyroxine should not be used to treat obesity or weight problems.
Dangerous side effects or death can occur from the misuse of this medicine.
This risk is especially high if you are taking other weight-loss medications.
This risk is especially high if you are taking appetite suppressants.
Taking more than your recommended dose will not make this medicine more effective.
Taking more than your recommended dose may cause serious side effects.
Levothyroxine has a narrow therapeutic index.
This means the difference between too little and too much is small.
Taking too much or too little over time can affect your heart.
It can affect your bones.
It can affect your blood sugar.
It can affect your cholesterol.
It can affect your digestion.
It can affect your memory and concentration.
It can affect your fertility.
In children, it can affect growth and development.
Your doctor will start you on a suitable dose and adjust it gradually based on blood tests.
You may not be able to use levothyroxine if you have certain medical conditions.

Blood tests, biotin, and monitoring:
Your doctor will use blood tests to check that your dose is right.
This is usually done 6 to 8 weeks after any dose change.
Then, blood tests are performed every 6 to 12 months once your dose is stable.
Children are tested more often.
They are tested 2 and 4 weeks after starting treatment.
They are also tested 2 weeks after any dose change.
Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you take biotin, or a multivitamin, hair, skin, or nail supplement that contains biotin (sometimes listed as vitamin B7).
Biotin can interfere with thyroid blood tests.
This interference can give a falsely high or falsely low result.
This could lead to the wrong dose change.
Stop biotin and any biotin-containing supplements at least 2 days before a thyroid blood test.
If your symptoms and blood tests still suggest an underactive thyroid even though you are on a dose that should be enough, it may be because the medicine is not being absorbed properly.
It may be because doses are being missed.
It may be because another medicine is interfering.

Lisinopril can harm your kidneys.
This risk is especially high if you also use certain medicines.
These medicines are for infections, cancer, or osteoporosis.
Tell your doctor about all your other medicines, especially:
a diuretic or "water pill" that may increase blood potassium such as spironolactone, triamterene, or amiloride;
NSAIDs (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) - aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), celecoxib, diclofenac, indomethacin, meloxicam, and others;
insulin or diabetes medications;
medicine to prevent organ transplant rejection such as temsirolimus, sirolimus, or everolimus; or
heart or blood pressure medication
lithium
gold injections.
This list is not complete.
Other drugs may interact with lisinopril.
These include prescription and over-the-counter medicines.
These also include vitamins and herbal products.
Not all possible drug interactions are listed here.

object: you may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088
relation_definition: The subject drug should be taken or used in the manner specified by the object entity (for example with food or at a fixed time).
evidence_text:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to lisinopril.
Signs of an allergic reaction to lisinopril include severe stomach pain, hives, difficult breathing, and swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.
Lisinopril may cause serious side effects.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
a light-headed feeling, like you might pass out;
high blood potassium - nausea, weakness, tingly feeling, chest pain, irregular heartbeats, loss of movement;
low white blood cell counts - fever, mouth sores, skin sores, sore throat, cough;
kidney problems - swelling, urinating less, feeling tired or short of breath; or
liver problems - loss of appetite, stomach pain (upper right side), tiredness, itching, dark urine, clay-colored stools, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or eyes).
Common lisinopril side effects may include:
headache, dizziness;
low blood pressure, cough; or
chest pain.
This is not a complete list of side effects and others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

evidence_text:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to lisinopril.
Signs of an allergic reaction to lisinopril include severe stomach pain, hives, difficult breathing, and swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.
Lisinopril may cause serious side effects.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
a light-headed feeling, like you might pass out;
high blood potassium - nausea, weakness, tingly feeling, chest pain, irregular heartbeats, loss of movement;
low white blood cell counts - fever, mouth sores, skin sores, sore throat, cough;
kidney problems - swelling, urinating less, feeling tired or short of breath; or
liver problems - loss of appetite, stomach pain (upper right side), tiredness, itching, dark urine, clay-colored stools, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or eyes).
Common lisinopril side effects may include:
headache, dizziness;
low blood pressure, cough; or
chest pain.
This is not a complete list of side effects and others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

subject: Lisinopril
relation_definition: The subject drug carries a safety warning or precaution about the risk or situation specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Take lisinopril exactly as prescribed by your doctor.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Your doctor may occasionally change your dose..
You may take lisinopril with or without food.
Measure liquid medicine with the supplied measuring device (not a kitchen spoon).
Your blood pressure will need to be checked often.
You may need frequent blood tests.
Tell your doctor if you have a planned surgery.
Call your doctor if you have ongoing vomiting or diarrhea, or if you are sweating more than usual.
You can easily become dehydrated while taking lisinopril.
This can lead to very low blood pressure, an electrolyte imbalance, or kidney failure.
If you have high blood pressure, keep using lisinopril even if you feel well.
High blood pressure often has no symptoms.
Store tightly closed at room temperature, away from moisture and heat.
Do not freeze.

evidence_text:
Lisinopril can harm your kidneys.
This risk is especially high if you also use certain medicines.
These medicines are for infections, cancer, or osteoporosis.
Tell your doctor about all your other medicines, especially:
a diuretic or "water pill" that may increase blood potassium such as spironolactone, triamterene, or amiloride;
NSAIDs (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) - aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), celecoxib, diclofenac, indomethacin, meloxicam, and others;
insulin or diabetes medications;
medicine to prevent organ transplant rejection such as temsirolimus, sirolimus, or everolimus; or
heart or blood pressure medication
lithium
gold injections.
This list is not complete.
Other drugs may interact with lisinopril.
These include prescription and over-the-counter medicines.
These also include vitamins and herbal products.
Not all possible drug interactions are listed here.

It could harm the unborn baby.
Stop using this medicine and tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant.

Usual Adult Dose for Myocardial Infarction:
The initial dose is 5 mg orally within 24 hours of the onset of acute myocardial infarction.
Subsequent doses are 5 mg orally after 24 hours.
Then, the dose is 10 mg orally after 48 hours.
Maintenance dose: 10 mg orally once a day.
Dosing should continue for at least 6 weeks.
Therapy should be initiated at 2.5 mg.
This applies to patients with a low systolic blood pressure.
The low systolic blood pressure is defined as less than or equal to 120 mm Hg and greater than 100 mmHg.
Therapy should be initiated during the first 3 days after the infarct.
Therapy should be withdrawn.
This occurs if prolonged hypotension happens.
Prolonged hypotension is defined as a systolic blood pressure less than 90 mmHg for more than 1 hour.
Uses: Reduction of mortality in acute myocardial infarction
Usual Adult Dose for Diabetic Nephropathy:
The initial dose is 10 to 20 mg orally once a day.
The maintenance dose is 20 to 40 mg orally once a day.
The dosage may be titrated upward every 3 days.
This is not an approved indication.

Tell your doctor if you have a planned surgery.

Store tightly closed at room temperature, away from moisture and heat.
Do not freeze.

Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning a pregnancy, or breastfeeding.
Studies published to date have not shown a link between metoprolol taken in pregnancy and major birth defects or miscarriage.
Reports on growth restriction, early birth, and death around the time of birth have been inconsistent.
Those studies have limitations that make them hard to interpret.
Untreated high blood pressure and untreated heart failure in pregnancy carry their own serious risks for both mother and baby.
Babies born to mothers taking metoprolol may have low blood pressure, low blood sugar, a slow heartbeat, or slow breathing.
So, they are watched after birth.
The amount of metoprolol a breastfed baby receives is estimated at 0.05 mg to under 1 mg a day.
This amount is about 0.5% to 2% of the mother's weight-adjusted dose.
No side effects in breastfed babies have been identified.
Babies are still monitored for a slow heartbeat and for signs such as unusual sleepiness.

subject: Metoprolol
object: blocking the effect of adrenaline and noradrenaline on beta-1 receptors in your heart
relation_definition: The subject drug has a specific effect or behavior in the group of individuals specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Metoprolol is a beta-blocker medication.
Metoprolol is used to treat high blood pressure.
Metoprolol is used to treat chest pain (angina).
Metoprolol is used to treat heart failure.
Metoprolol is used to improve survival after a heart attack.
It works mainly on the heart.
It is called a cardioselective beta-blocker.
Metoprolol works by blocking the effect of adrenaline and noradrenaline on beta-1 receptors in your heart.
This slows your heart rate.
It reduces how hard your heart squeezes.
It lowers your blood pressure.
The heart is doing less work.
Because the heart is doing less work, it needs less oxygen.
Metoprolol helps with angina.
Metoprolol helps with angina because the heart needs less oxygen.
Exactly how metoprolol works is not fully understood.
Metoprolol is used for high blood pressure, heart failure, and after a heart attack.
At higher blood levels, metoprolol also blocks beta-2 receptors in the airways and blood vessels.
This is why it still needs care in people with breathing problems.

relation_definition: The subject drug has a specific effect or behavior in the group of individuals specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
The most important warning with metoprolol is not to stop it suddenly.
Stopping a beta blocker abruptly can bring on worse chest pain.
In some cases, it can bring on a heart attack.
If your treatment needs to stop, your prescriber will lower the dose gradually over 1 to 2 weeks.
Your prescriber will watch how you respond.
This applies even if you only take metoprolol for blood pressure.
Heart disease is common.
Heart disease is not always known about.
Talk to your care team before starting metoprolol if any of these apply to you.
Asthma or other breathing problems.
Beta blockers can tighten the airways.
Metoprolol is used in people with these conditions only when other treatments are not suitable.
It is used at the lowest possible dose.
A reliever inhaler is kept on hand.
Heart failure.
Heart failure can get worse while the dose is being increased.
Tell your doctor about weight gain or increasing breathlessness.
A slow heart rate or a conduction problem in the heart.
This includes first-degree heart block, sinus node problems, and Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome.

evidence_text:
Metoprolol crosses the placenta and passes into breast milk in small amounts.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning a pregnancy, or breastfeeding.
Studies published to date have not shown a link between metoprolol taken in pregnancy and major birth defects or miscarriage.
Reports on growth restriction, early birth, and death around the time of birth have been inconsistent.
Those studies have limitations that make them hard to interpret.
Untreated high blood pressure and untreated heart failure in pregnancy carry their own serious risks for both mother and baby.
Babies born to mothers taking metoprolol may have low blood pressure, low blood sugar, a slow heartbeat, or slow breathing.
So, they are watched after birth.
The amount of metoprolol a breastfed baby receives is estimated at 0.05 mg to under 1 mg a day.
This amount is about 0.5% to 2% of the mother's weight-adjusted dose.
No side effects in breastfed babies have been identified.
Babies are still monitored for a slow heartbeat and for signs such as unusual sleepiness.

nausea, vomiting, diarrhea; or

subject: omeprazole
object: blocking the acid pump in your stomach
relation_definition: The subject drug has a specific effect or behavior in the group of individuals specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Omeprazole is used to treat excess stomach acid.
It is used in conditions such as stomach ulcers, heartburn, or gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).
It is used in active duodenal ulcer, Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, and erosive esophagitis.
Omeprazole may be given together with antibiotics.
This combination is used to treat gastric ulcers.
The ulcers are caused by infection with Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori).
The treatment is for adult patients.
Omeprazole is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI).
Omeprazole works by blocking the acid pump in your stomach.
This reduces how much acid the stomach makes.
This gives irritated or damaged tissue a chance to heal.
Omeprazole brand names are Prilosec, Prilosec OTC.
Generic brands are available.
Omeprazole is available over the counter (OTC) and as a prescription medication.

subject: Triple therapy
relation_definition: The subject therapy achieves the specified rate of eradication of the target condition.
evidence_text:
Triple therapy has resulted in eradication rates of greater than 95%.
The QUADRATE Study (n=405) involves quadruple therapy.
This therapy consists of 40 mg of the primary drug taken orally twice daily for 7 days.
It is administered concomitantly with bismuth subcitrate, taken four times daily.
It is also administered concomitantly with tetracycline, taken four times daily.
It includes metronidazole 200 mg taken three times daily.
It includes metronidazole 400 mg taken at bedtime.
Helicobacter Pylori eradication was achieved in 82% of patients.

subject: Rosuvastatin
relation_definition: The subject drug was approved by the US FDA in the year specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Rosuvastatin (Crestor) is a prescription medicine.
The medicine is used to treat high cholesterol.
The medicine is used to reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events.
Major cardiovascular events include heart attack and stroke.
Rosuvastatin belongs to a class of medicines called statins.
It works by blocking HMG-CoA reductase.
HMG-CoA reductase is the rate-limiting enzyme the liver uses to make cholesterol.
With cholesterol synthesis reduced, the liver increases its LDL receptors.
The liver clears more LDL from the blood.
LDL is "bad" cholesterol.
LDL and total cholesterol levels fall.
The maximum reduction is usually reached by four weeks.
Rosuvastatin comes as a tablet.
It was first approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on August 12, 2003.
It was approved under the brand name Crestor.
Many generic versions of rosuvastatin tablets have since been approved.

subject: Rosuvastatin
relation_definition: The subject drug has a specific effect or behavior in the group of individuals specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Rosuvastatin (Crestor) is a prescription medicine.
The medicine is used to treat high cholesterol.
The medicine is used to reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events.
Major cardiovascular events include heart attack and stroke.
Rosuvastatin belongs to a class of medicines called statins.
It works by blocking HMG-CoA reductase.
HMG-CoA reductase is the rate-limiting enzyme the liver uses to make cholesterol.
With cholesterol synthesis reduced, the liver increases its LDL receptors.
The liver clears more LDL from the blood.
LDL is "bad" cholesterol.
LDL and total cholesterol levels fall.
The maximum reduction is usually reached by four weeks.
Rosuvastatin comes as a tablet.
It was first approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on August 12, 2003.
It was approved under the brand name Crestor.
Many generic versions of rosuvastatin tablets have since been approved.

subject: Rosuvastatin
relation_definition: The subject product is categorized as the product type specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Rosuvastatin (Crestor) is a prescription medicine.
The medicine is used to treat high cholesterol.
The medicine is used to reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events.
Major cardiovascular events include heart attack and stroke.
Rosuvastatin belongs to a class of medicines called statins.
It works by blocking HMG-CoA reductase.
HMG-CoA reductase is the rate-limiting enzyme the liver uses to make cholesterol.
With cholesterol synthesis reduced, the liver increases its LDL receptors.
The liver clears more LDL from the blood.
LDL is "bad" cholesterol.
LDL and total cholesterol levels fall.
The maximum reduction is usually reached by four weeks.
Rosuvastatin comes as a tablet.
It was first approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on August 12, 2003.
It was approved under the brand name Crestor.
Many generic versions of rosuvastatin tablets have since been approved.

subject: major cardiovascular events
relation_definition: The subject condition or category includes the specific condition or entity specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Rosuvastatin (Crestor) is a prescription medicine.
The medicine is used to treat high cholesterol.
The medicine is used to reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events.
Major cardiovascular events include heart attack and stroke.
Rosuvastatin belongs to a class of medicines called statins.
It works by blocking HMG-CoA reductase.
HMG-CoA reductase is the rate-limiting enzyme the liver uses to make cholesterol.
With cholesterol synthesis reduced, the liver increases its LDL receptors.
The liver clears more LDL from the blood.
LDL is "bad" cholesterol.
LDL and total cholesterol levels fall.
The maximum reduction is usually reached by four weeks.
Rosuvastatin comes as a tablet.
It was first approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on August 12, 2003.
It was approved under the brand name Crestor.
Many generic versions of rosuvastatin tablets have since been approved.

Tell your doctor about all the medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements.
Also tell the doctor who prescribes rosuvastatin if another doctor increases the dose of another medicine you are taking.
Rosuvastatin may affect the way other medicines work.
Other medicines may affect how rosuvastatin works.

coumarin anticoagulants (medicines that prevent blood clots, such as warfarin)
antacids (medicines you take for heartburn that contain aluminum and magnesium hydroxide)

cyclosporine (a medicine for your immune system)

enasidenib (a medicine used to treat acute myeloid leukemia)
capmatinib (a medicine for the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer)
fostamatinib (a medicine used to treat low platelet counts)

These side effects may occur in people with type 2 diabetes.
One specific side effect in people with type 2 diabetes is low blood sugar.
Stomach or gastrointestinal side effects are common.
They tend to be mild and clear up in a few weeks.

Eat smaller meals

Eat foods that contain water (like soup or gelatin)
Do not lie down right after eating
Drink clear or ice-cold liquids

evidence_text:
You should not use semaglutide if you are allergic to it, or if you have:
multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 (tumors in your glands);
a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma (a type of thyroid cancer); or
diabetic ketoacidosis (call your doctor for treatment).
Tell your doctor if you have ever had:
a stomach or intestinal disorder;
pancreatitis;
are planning surgery or other procedure that uses anesthesia or deep sedation;
kidney disease; or
eye problems caused by diabetes (retinopathy).
In animal studies, semaglutide caused thyroid tumors or thyroid cancer.
It is not known whether these effects would occur in people.
Ask your doctor about your risk.
Pregnancy:
Men and women should stop using semaglutide at least 2 months before they plan to get pregnant.
Ask your doctor for a safer medicine to use during this time.
Controlling diabetes is very important during pregnancy.
Gaining the right amount of weight is also very important during pregnancy.
Even if you are overweight, losing weight during pregnancy could harm the unborn baby.

relation_definition: The subject drug requires the recommended action specified by the object entity in response to a serious side effect.
evidence_text:
Depression itself raises the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors.
Anyone taking sertraline should be watched closely.
They should be watched for worsening symptoms.
They should be watched for new or sudden changes in mood, behavior, thoughts, or feelings.
This monitoring is especially important in the first few months of treatment.
This monitoring is also important whenever the dose is changed.
Call your healthcare provider right away, or call 911 in an emergency, if you notice:
thoughts about suicide or dying, or attempts to harm yourself
new or worse depression, anxiety, or panic attacks
feeling agitated, restless, angry, or irritable
acting aggressive or violent, or acting on dangerous impulses
trouble sleeping
a big increase in activity or talking more than is normal for you
any other unusual change in behavior or mood
Tell family members or caregivers which symptoms to watch for, so they can call your provider if you are not able to.

subject: exclusively breastfed infants
relation_definition: The subject group has a specific level or concentration of the subject drug, as specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Breastfeeding:
Low levels of sertraline and its breakdown products pass into breast milk.
A pooled analysis of 53 mother and infant pairs was conducted.
Exclusively breastfed infants had an average of 2% of the sertraline levels measured in their mothers' blood.
The levels ranged from 0% to 15%.
No side effects were seen in those infants.
There is no information on whether sertraline affects milk production.
Talk with your doctor about the benefits of breastfeeding alongside your need for treatment.
Children:
Sertraline is approved for OCD in children aged 6 to 17 years.
It is not known to be safe and effective in children under 6.
It is not known to be safe and effective for any other condition in this age group.
Children and teenagers taking sertraline should be monitored for worsening symptoms and suicidal thoughts.
This monitoring is especially important early in treatment and when the dose changes.
Their weight and growth should be checked.
Older adults:
Older adults clear sertraline more slowly.

subject: sertraline oral solution
object: store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C)
relation_definition: The subject drug should be stored according to the instruction specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Take sertraline exactly as prescribed, once a day, in either the morning or the evening.
Take it at around the same time each day.
Tablets and capsules can be taken with or without food.
Taking sertraline with food causes only a small increase in the amount absorbed.
Swallow capsules whole.
Do not open, crush, or chew them.
Your doctor may start you on a low dose and raise it gradually.
This is usually done no more often than once a week.
Keep taking sertraline even if you feel well.
Do not stop without talking to your doctor first.
Tell any doctor or lab that you take sertraline before you have tests.
Sertraline can cause a false-positive result on urine screening tests for benzodiazepines.
This can continue for several days after you stop taking it.
A confirmatory test will tell the difference.
Store sertraline at room temperature, 68°F to 77°F (20°C to 25°C).
How to take sertraline oral solution:
Sertraline oral solution must be diluted before you take it.
Do not mix it in advance.
Use the dropper supplied with the bottle.

subject: sertraline 150 mg capsule
relation_definition: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
The oral solution specifically is not recommended in pregnancy because it contains alcohol.
What are sertraline 150 mg and 200 mg capsules for?
:
Sertraline capsules come in 150 mg and 200 mg only.
They are not used to start treatment.
They are for people who have already been taking 100 mg or 125 mg of another sertraline product for at least a week and need a higher dose.
The maximum is 200 mg a day, the same as for tablets.
Capsules should be swallowed whole and not opened, crushed, or chewed.
If you need to come off sertraline, the dose has to be lowered gradually.
This must be done using another sertraline product.
There is no capsule strength below 150 mg.
Capsules are approved for depression in adults.
Capsules are approved for OCD from age 6.
Capsules are not approved for panic disorder.
Capsules are not approved for PTSD.
Capsules are not approved for social anxiety disorder.
Capsules are not approved for PMDD.
Does sertraline interact with warfarin?
:
Yes, in two ways.
Sertraline can add to warfarin's effect on bleeding risk.

subject: pimozide
relation_definition: The medical condition specified by the subject may present with the symptom specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Several medicines interact with sertraline.
Give a full list of everything you take to any provider who treats you.
The most important interactions are:
MAOIs.
Taking sertraline with an MAOI raises the risk of serotonin syndrome.
The combination is contraindicated.
Examples include selegiline, tranylcypromine, isocarboxazid, phenelzine, linezolid, and methylene blue.
Pimozide.
Sertraline raises pimozide levels.
This can lead to QTc prolongation.
This can lead to irregular heartbeats.
The combination is contraindicated.
Other medicines that raise serotonin.
These add to the risk of serotonin syndrome.
Examples include other SSRIs and SNRIs.
Examples include triptans for migraine.
Examples include tricyclic antidepressants.
Examples include opioids.
Examples include lithium.
Examples include tryptophan.
Examples include buspirone.
Examples include amphetamines.
Examples include St. John's wort.
Blood thinners and antiplatelet medicines.
Aspirin, clopidogrel, heparin, and warfarin can add to the bleeding risk.
If you take warfarin, your INR should be monitored carefully.

Can sertraline cause diarrhea or nausea?

Nausea was reported by 26% of people taking sertraline in trials, compared with 12% on placebo.

:

evidence_text:
Common sertraline side effects:
The most common sertraline side effects are nausea, diarrhea or loose stools.
They include trouble sleeping, dry mouth, and tiredness.
They also include dizziness, sleepiness, tremor, and indigestion.
Other common side effects are agitation, reduced appetite, increased sweating, and sexual problems.
The table below shows how often each side effect was reported.
The data comes from pooled placebo-controlled trials.
The trials included 3,066 adults.
The trials included 2,293 people taking placebo.
Side effect | Sertraline | Placebo
Nausea | 26% | 12%
Diarrhea or loose stools | 20% | 10%
Insomnia (trouble sleeping) | 20% | 13%
Dry mouth | 14% | 9%
Fatigue (tiredness) | 12% | 8%
Dizziness | 12% | 8%
Somnolence (sleepiness) | 11% | 6%
Tremor (shaking) | 9% | 2%
Dyspepsia (indigestion) | 8% | 4%
Agitation | 8% | 5%
Decreased appetite | 7% | 2%
Hyperhidrosis (heavy sweating) | 7% | 3%
Constipation | 6% | 4%
Decreased libido (lower sex drive) | 6% | 2%
Palpitations | 4% | 2%
Visual impairment | 4% | 2%
Vomiting | 4% | 1%

subject: Pooled analyses
relation_definition: The subject entity is identified as or is equivalent to the object entity.
evidence_text:
Sertraline carries a boxed warning, the FDA's most serious type of warning.
Antidepressants increased the risk of suicidal thoughts and behavior in children, teenagers, and young adults in short-term studies.
Pooled analyses of placebo-controlled antidepressant trials were conducted.
The trials covered about 77,000 adults and more than 4,500 children and teenagers.
The risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in people aged 24 and under was higher with an antidepressant than with placebo.
The risk varied considerably between different antidepressants.
The risk also varied by condition.
The highest rate was in people being treated for depression.
The difference between antidepressant and placebo, per 1,000 patients treated, was:
Age (years) | Difference compared with placebo
Under 18 | 14 more patients with suicidal thoughts or behaviors
18 to 24 | 5 more patients
25 to 64 | 1 fewer patient
65 and over | 6 fewer patients
It is not known whether this risk continues beyond about four months of treatment.
There is good evidence that antidepressants delay depression coming back in adults.

Sertraline carries a boxed warning, the FDA's most serious type of warning.

Several medicines interact with sertraline.
Give a full list of everything you take to any provider who treats you.
The most important interactions are:
MAOIs.
Taking sertraline with an MAOI raises the risk of serotonin syndrome.
The combination is contraindicated.
Examples include selegiline, tranylcypromine, isocarboxazid, phenelzine, linezolid, and methylene blue.
Pimozide.
Sertraline raises pimozide levels.
This can lead to QTc prolongation.
This can lead to irregular heartbeats.
The combination is contraindicated.
Other medicines that raise serotonin.
These add to the risk of serotonin syndrome.
Examples include other SSRIs and SNRIs.
Examples include triptans for migraine.
Examples include tricyclic antidepressants.
Examples include opioids.
Examples include lithium.
Examples include tryptophan.
Examples include buspirone.
Examples include amphetamines.
Examples include St. John's wort.
Blood thinners and antiplatelet medicines.
Aspirin, clopidogrel, heparin, and warfarin can add to the bleeding risk.
If you take warfarin, your INR should be monitored carefully.

How long does sertraline take to work?
:
Sertraline levels in the blood become steady after about a week of once daily dosing.
The effect on symptoms takes longer.
The trials that established sertraline ran for 6 to 12 weeks.
These trials were for depression.
These trials were for OCD.
These trials were for panic disorder.
These trials were for PTSD.
These trials were for social anxiety disorder.
The trials ran for over three menstrual cycles.
These trials were for PMDD.
This duration gives a sense of the time frame over which the benefit was measured.
It takes time.
Doses are usually raised no more often than once a week.
You should keep taking sertraline even if you do not feel a change yet.
How long does sertraline stay in your system?
:
Sertraline has a half-life of about 26 hours.
This means half of what is in your blood is cleared in roughly a day.
At that rate, most of a dose has left your bloodstream within about 5 to 6 days.
Its main breakdown product, N-desmethylsertraline, lasts longer.
It has a half-life of 62 to 104 hours.
It is much less active than sertraline itself.

subject: Risk

evidence_text:
Sertraline carries a boxed warning, the FDA's most serious type of warning.
Antidepressants increased the risk of suicidal thoughts and behavior in children, teenagers, and young adults in short-term studies.
Pooled analyses of placebo-controlled antidepressant trials were conducted.
The trials covered about 77,000 adults and more than 4,500 children and teenagers.
The risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in people aged 24 and under was higher with an antidepressant than with placebo.
The risk varied considerably between different antidepressants.
The risk also varied by condition.
The highest rate was in people being treated for depression.
The difference between antidepressant and placebo, per 1,000 patients treated, was:
Age (years) | Difference compared with placebo
Under 18 | 14 more patients with suicidal thoughts or behaviors
18 to 24 | 5 more patients
25 to 64 | 1 fewer patient
65 and over | 6 fewer patients
It is not known whether this risk continues beyond about four months of treatment.
There is good evidence that antidepressants delay depression coming back in adults.

Low levels of sertraline and its breakdown products pass into breast milk.
A pooled analysis of 53 mother and infant pairs was conducted.
Exclusively breastfed infants had an average of 2% of the sertraline levels measured in their mothers' blood.
The levels ranged from 0% to 15%.
No side effects were seen in those infants.
There is no information on whether sertraline affects milk production.
Talk with your doctor about the benefits of breastfeeding alongside your need for treatment.
Children:
Sertraline is approved for OCD in children aged 6 to 17 years.
It is not known to be safe and effective in children under 6.
It is not known to be safe and effective for any other condition in this age group.

Sertraline is FDA-approved to treat six conditions in adults:
Major depressive disorder (MDD), the clinical term for depression.
Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), where unwanted thoughts drive repeated behaviors.
Panic disorder, which causes sudden attacks of intense fear along with physical symptoms.
Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), which can follow a frightening or traumatic event.
Social anxiety disorder (SAD), also called social phobia.
Premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), a severe form of premenstrual symptoms.
In children and teenagers, sertraline is approved only for OCD, from age 6 upward.
Its safety and effectiveness have not been established in children under 6 years of age.
Its safety and effectiveness have not been established in children and teenagers for any condition other than OCD.
Not every sertraline product is approved for all six conditions:
Sertraline tablets and oral solution are approved for all of them.
Sertraline 150 mg and 200 mg capsules are approved only for depression in adults and for OCD in adults and children aged 6 and over.

Get medical help straight away if this happens, because without prompt treatment it can lead to permanent erectile dysfunction.
An enlarged prostate and prostate cancer can occur together.
Ask your doctor about prostate cancer screening before you start tamsulosin and at regular intervals while you are taking it.
Tamsulosin can cause a problem called intraoperative floppy iris syndrome (IFIS) during cataract or glaucoma surgery.
Tell your eye surgeon that you take tamsulosin or have taken it in the past, even if you stopped months ago.
Do not stop taking tamsulosin before surgery unless your surgeon tells you to.
Starting tamsulosin is not recommended.
This applies if you are already booked in for cataract or glaucoma surgery.
If you stop taking tamsulosin for several days, talk to your doctor before starting again.
You will need to restart at the 0.4 mg dose.
Many other medicines can interact with tamsulosin.
Tell your doctor about everything you take, including prescription medicines, over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.

subject: medications
relation_definition: The object condition or situation increases the likelihood of the subject condition occurring.
evidence_text:
Tamsulosin is broken down in the body mainly by two liver enzymes, CYP3A4 and CYP2D6.
Medicines that block these enzymes can raise the amount of tamsulosin in your blood.
These medicines can increase the risk of side effects.
The medicines block these enzymes.
Do not take tamsulosin with:
strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as ketoconazole
other alpha blockers, such as alfuzosin, doxazosin, prazosin, silodosin, or terazosin
Use with caution, and tell your doctor if you take:
moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as erythromycin
strong CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as paroxetine, or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as terbinafine
cimetidine
warfarin
medicines for erectile dysfunction or pulmonary arterial hypertension known as PDE5 inhibitors, including avanafil (Stendra), sildenafil (Viagra, Revatio), tadalafil (Adcirca, Cialis), and vardenafil (Levitra).
Taking these with tamsulosin can lower blood pressure enough to cause symptoms.
Some of these cautions matter more at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at 0.4 mg.
Your doctor will decide what is right for you.

subject: Tamsulosin
relation_definition: The subject drug has a drug interaction with the drug or substance specified by the object entity that may change effects or cause harm.
evidence_text:
Do not take tamsulosin if you are allergic to tamsulosin or to any of the ingredients in the capsule.
Do not take tamsulosin with other alpha blockers.
Examples of other alpha blockers include alfuzosin (Uroxatral), doxazosin (Cardura), prazosin (Minipress), silodosin (Rapaflo), and terazosin (Hytrin).
Do not take tamsulosin 0.4 mg with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor such as ketoconazole.
These medicines raise tamsulosin levels in your blood.
Tamsulosin can lower your blood pressure when you stand up.
This may make you feel dizzy or faint.
This is most likely when you first start taking it.
This is most likely when your dose changes.
This is most likely when you start it again after a break.
Get up slowly from sitting or lying down.
Be careful driving or doing anything that needs you to be alert until you know how tamsulosin affects you.
In rare cases, tamsulosin can cause priapism.
These cases probably occur in fewer than 1 in 50,000 patients.
Priapism is a painful erection that lasts a long time.
Priapism is not related to sexual activity.

Do not take tamsulosin if you are allergic to tamsulosin or to any of the ingredients in the capsule.

Priapism is a painful erection that lasts a long time.
Priapism is not related to sexual activity.

subject: Tamsulosin
relation_definition: The subject drug is not indicated or used to treat or manage the condition or situation specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Tamsulosin is used to treat the symptoms of an enlarged prostate, also called benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH.
These symptoms include a weak urine stream.
They include trouble starting to urinate.
They include dribbling.
They include a feeling of not emptying the bladder completely.
They include needing to urinate often or urgently.
They include getting up at night to urinate.
Tamsulosin belongs to a group of medicines called alpha blockers.
It works by blocking alpha-1 receptors in the prostate and bladder neck.
Blocking these receptors relaxes the muscle there.
This improves urine flow and eases BPH symptoms.
Tamsulosin is taken once daily, about half an hour after the same meal each day.
Capsules should be swallowed whole and not crushed, chewed, or opened.
The tamsulosin brand name was Flomax.
Flomax has now been discontinued in the U.S.
Generic tamsulosin is available.
Tamsulosin is not approved to treat high blood pressure.
It is not approved for use in women or children.

subject: Tamsulosin
relation_definition: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition or characteristic specified by the object entity.
evidence_text:
Tamsulosin is broken down in the body mainly by two liver enzymes, CYP3A4 and CYP2D6.
Medicines that block these enzymes can raise the amount of tamsulosin in your blood.
These medicines can increase the risk of side effects.
The medicines block these enzymes.
Do not take tamsulosin with:
strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as ketoconazole
other alpha blockers, such as alfuzosin, doxazosin, prazosin, silodosin, or terazosin
Use with caution, and tell your doctor if you take:
moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as erythromycin
strong CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as paroxetine, or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as terbinafine
cimetidine
warfarin
medicines for erectile dysfunction or pulmonary arterial hypertension known as PDE5 inhibitors, including avanafil (Stendra), sildenafil (Viagra, Revatio), tadalafil (Adcirca, Cialis), and vardenafil (Levitra).
Taking these with tamsulosin can lower blood pressure enough to cause symptoms.
Some of these cautions matter more at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at 0.4 mg.
Your doctor will decide what is right for you.

-This drug should be taken shortly after a meal or light snack.

Trazodone is an antidepressant that belongs to a group of drugs called serotonin receptor antagonists and reuptake inhibitors (SARIs).
Trazodone is not a true member of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) class of antidepressants.
Trazodone shares many properties of the SSRIs.
Trazodone is used to treat major depressive disorder.
It may help to improve your mood.
It may help to improve your appetite.
It may help to improve your energy level.
It may help to decrease anxiety related to depression.
It may help to decrease insomnia related to depression.
Trazodone works by helping to restore the balance of a certain natural chemical (serotonin) in the brain.
